_comment: KPI definitions. Each is a row in kpi_definition; every computed value
records the version that produced it, so any historical result traces to
ON PROVENANCE (§486). All three are definitional ratios from standard
Indian utility practice, not physics invented here:
gross unit heat rate  = coal flow (t/h) x 1000 kg/t x GCV (kcal/kg)
auxiliary power       = aux power / gross generation x 100   [%]
specific coal         = coal flow (t/h) x 1000 kg/t / (MW x 1000 kW)
None requires a steam table. Cylinder efficiency and condenser performance
DO, so under §486 they are not implemented rather than approximated.
The GCV constant is a stated assumption, not a measurement: this
demonstrator has no coal analysis. On a real unit it comes from the daily
laboratory result, and heat rate is only as good as it is.
inputs map an equation variable to an ATTRIBUTE name, resolved through the
asset model, so the same definition serves every unit.

definitions.name: GrossUnitHeatRate
definitions.description: Gross unit heat rate: heat input per unit of electrical output. Coal flow times gross calorific value, divided by gross generation.

definitions.name: AuxiliaryPowerConsumption
definitions.description: Auxiliary power consumption as a percentage of gross generation.

definitions.name: SpecificCoalConsumption
definitions.description: Coal consumed per unit of electrical output.
